Where it began

Cooper Patrick Leonard Connolly was born on 22 August 2003 and came through the Western Australian ranks. He was a leader from the start: he captained the state's under-17 side and, in January 2022, was named captain of Australia at the Under-19 World Cup.

The Perth Scorchers signed him that August, and he made his Twenty20 debut for them in January 2023. He did not wait long to make a mark. In the Big Bash final that season his 25 off 11 balls settled the match in the Scorchers' favour.

The player

He bats left-handed and bowls orthodox left-arm spin. His first-class debut, in March 2024, came in nothing smaller than a Sheffield Shield final, against Tasmania, and he made 90 in the first innings.

International cricket followed quickly. In September 2024 he made his Twenty20 international debut against Scotland and his one-day debut against England. In January 2025 he played his first Test, the second of the series in Sri Lanka, and was handed his Baggy Green, the 471st, by Simon Katich, another West Australian all-rounder. By November 2026 he had played 2 Tests, made 33 runs and taken his first Test wicket.

What made him special

He does a bit of everything, and does it when it matters. In 2025, against South Africa, he became the youngest Australian to take five wickets in a one-day international. In June 2026 in Mirpur he made his first international hundred, 149 from 134 balls against Bangladesh, well over half of the 275 his side needed to win.

By November 2026 his Test career was a short one, a first taste rather than a full meal, and his highest Test score was 29. Given how quickly the rest has come, few would bet against more.

Away from the middle

He has said he models himself on Shaun Marsh, the former Australia batsman and, like him, a West Australian. By November 2026 he had played his domestic cricket for Western Australia, his Big Bash cricket for the Perth Scorchers, and had a place with the Punjab Kings in the Indian Premier League.

And finally

His first-class career began with a Shield final, his first international hundred carried a run chase, and his first big moment for the Scorchers won a title. Somebody should tell him that most players have to start small.
